title: Sharp local stability of Ptolemaic split metrics
shortTitle: How sharply does a metric leave equality?
oneLine: Exact first-order rates describe how the negative-type gap opens near every specified split metric, with a different, quadratic transition at four points.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate determines sharp lower and upper first-order stability constants at the binding complete split metrics of every cardinality at least six, and at the five-point split. A nonlinear realisation lemma identifies the exact tangent cone; 18 rational-function dual families and 36 small certificates establish sharp cone constants. The paper derives explicit quadratic remainders and fixed-cardinality sensitivity of the supremal negative-type exponent. Unequal arms at the four-point star instead give a quadratic gap. Global equality completeness and collision consequences retain their separate companion/source dependencies.
narration: An exact mathematical boundary raises a second question: how quickly do things change when we move away from it? This research studies finite collections of distances called Ptolemaic metrics. They satisfy the triangle inequality and an additional four-point inequality. A previous candidate identified a sharp negative-type threshold. At that threshold, special split metrics sit exactly on an equality boundary. The new work asks what happens when their distances change slightly. Its main result gives the smallest and largest possible first-order rates at which the negative-type gap opens. These rates are exact, not estimates from random sampling. They depend on how many points lie on each side of the split. The units matter: the mean distance between the two parts is fixed at one, and the size of a perturbation is its largest change in any distance. The proof first identifies all feasible infinitesimal directions. It then shows that each can be realised by actual Ptolemaic metrics, with a small quadratic correction. Eighteen symbolic certificate families cover arbitrarily large sizes, while thirty-six small certificates handle the exceptions. Four points behave differently. Changing the arms of a particular star opens the gap quadratically, so the same positive linear lower bound cannot apply there. This is a local stability result, not a universal robustness guarantee for all metrics. The archive includes proofs, complete certificate tables, corrected verification code and replay records. It remains an unrefereed candidate, without formal or external verification. This is Evidence Press, Ptolemaic split stability, released on the twenty-seventh of September twenty twenty-six, version zero point three point one candidate. The paper and evidence are linked on this page. This synthetic AI voice is an explanation, not additional scientific evidence.

problem.name: Sharp stability near complete split equality metrics

keyResults: Exact attained lower and upper first-order gap coefficients under mean-cross-distance-one and infinity-norm normalisation.
Three stable parity-dependent lower-coefficient formulas for cardinality at least nine; six small exceptions are handled exactly.
Every normalised linearised feasible direction is realised by a Ptolemaic curve with a quadratic inward correction.
Fixed-cardinality first variation of the supremal negative-type exponent; four-point unequal-arm perturbations give a quadratic gap instead.
Conditional collision-kernel characterisation and an explicit subcritical separated-metric gap bound; no general global stability constant is claimed.
evidence: Written proofs; all 18 universal symbolic dual families and 36 small certificates; pinned exact, symbolic and numerical replay; separate supplied checker rerun; semantic corruption controls across five Python modes; point-by-point review response.
